title: Domaino prediction API, version 1.0
description: Task T4.1's API contract: the one definition the model, backend and frontend all read. The backend validates every request and every response it emits against these schemas, so a contract violation fails a test rather than reaching a user. Breaking changes bump the major version and get a new path prefix (/api/v2); additive fields do not.

x-endpoints.description: Liveness plus which model is loaded. Safe to poll.
Submit a sequence. Returns immediately with a job; prediction runs in the background because ESM-2 inference on a long chain takes seconds to minutes.
Poll a job. The same shape throughout its life: `status` says whether `result` or `error` is present.
Forget a job and the sequence it carried. Part of the privacy commitment in WP4's objectives, and the reason a submitted sequence is never written anywhere else.

sequence.description: One protein sequence. A leading FASTA header line and any internal whitespace or case are accepted and normalised by the backend, which reports what it did in `result.warnings`; multi-record FASTA is rejected rather than silently truncated to the first record. This limit counts characters, not residues, because the field also carries the header and line breaks; the residue limit is 100,000 and exceeding it is reported as `sequence_too_long` rather than as a contract violation, which tells the user something they can act on.

name.description: Label shown in the interface. Defaults to the FASTA header, or to the job id.

architecture.description: Which trained segmentation model to use. Defaults to whichever won on validation mean IoU in WP3.

include_tracks.description: Return per-residue probabilities. The sequence view needs them for its confidence ribbon; a scripted caller usually does not, and they are one float per residue.

include_structure.description: Request optional structure prediction (T4.5). Never blocks the sequence-only result: if it fails, `result` still arrives and a warning explains the absence.

stage.description: Named stages rather than a percentage: the frontend shows what is happening, and a stage that stalls names itself.

Prediction.description: The inference-output schema of deliverable D2.3, as the API exposes it.

unassigned.description: Residues in no predicted domain: linkers, tails, and anything the decoder's coverage constraint left out. Present so the sequence view can colour every residue and never leave a silent gap.

tracks.description: Per-residue probabilities, same length as the sequence. Only when `options.include_tracks` was set.

warnings.description: Things the user should know that are not failures: a normalised sequence, a chain longer than ESM-2's training crop, an abstained superfamily, an unavailable optional service.

index.description: 1-based position in this prediction. Not a CATH domain number.

segments.description: More than one segment means a discontinuous domain, which the pairwise and query designs both represent and which a boundary-only model cannot.

confidence.description: Model confidence in the segmentation of this domain, not in its CATH label.

Segment.description: A 1-based inclusive residue interval into the submitted sequence. The same convention the dataset uses, so a result can be compared with CATH without re-indexing.

CathAssignment.description: Hierarchical label. C, A and T are always present; H may be unresolved, which is a result and not an error.

path.description: The chosen levels joined, e.g. `3.40.50.300`, truncated where the model abstained.

code.description: CATH code at this level, or null when unresolved.

name.description: Human-readable CATH name, when one is known.

status.description: `unresolved` with a `reason` whenever the model declined: too few training domains in that superfamily, or probability below the calibrated threshold.

ModelInfo.description: Which model produced this, in enough detail to reproduce it from the experiment registry.

mode.description: `mock` means the backend had no checkpoint and returned a plausible simulated result. The interface must label it, and no mock result may ever be presented as a prediction.

run_id.description: Run id in reports/experiments/, which carries the seed, config, revision and metrics.

selection.description: The validation metric the checkpoint was selected on.

retention.description: How long the backend keeps the submitted sequence and this result.

Error.description: Every failure says which of the two sides must change, in words a user can act on. WP4's objectives require clear errors rather than a bare status code.
